question: Identify the state abbreviations where, for both male and female legislators, the retention rate remains greater than zero at specific intervals of 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 years after their first term start date. A legislator is considered retained if they are serving on December 31 of the respective year. Only include states where both gender cohorts maintain non-zero retention rates at all six of these time points during the first decade of service.
sql:
-- Count total qualifying states
WITH first_terms AS (
    SELECT l.id_bioguide, l.gender, lt.state, CAST(lt.term_start AS DATE) as first_term_start
    FROM legislators l
    JOIN legislators_terms lt ON l.id_bioguide = lt.id_bioguide
    WHERE lt.term_number = 0
),
intervals AS (
    SELECT 0 as interval UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 10
),
retention_check AS (
    SELECT ft.id_bioguide, ft.gender, ft.state, ft.first_term_start, i.interval,
           (CAST(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM ft.first_term_start) AS INTEGER) + i.interval)::VARCHAR || '-12-31' as target_date_str
    FROM first_terms ft
    CROSS JOIN intervals i
),
retained AS (
    SELECT rc.id_bioguide, rc.gender, rc.state, rc.interval,
           CASE WHEN EXISTS (
               SELECT 1 FROM legislators_terms lt
               WHERE lt.id_bioguide = rc.id_bioguide
               AND CAST(lt.term_start AS DATE) <= CAST(rc.target_date_str AS DATE)
               AND (CAST(lt.term_end AS DATE) >= CAST(rc.target_date_str AS DATE) OR lt.term_end IS NULL)
           ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END as is_retained
    FROM retention_check rc
),
state_gender_retention AS (
    SELECT state, gender, interval, AVG(is_retained * 1.0) as retention_rate
    FROM retained
    GROUP BY state, gender, interval
),
state_gender_check AS (
    SELECT state, gender,
           MIN(retention_rate) as min_retention,
           COUNT(*) as intervals_checked
    FROM state_gender_retention
    GROUP BY state, gender
    HAVING MIN(retention_rate) > 0 AND COUNT(*) = 6
)
SELECT DISTINCT sgc.state
FROM state_gender_check sgc
WHERE sgc.gender IN ('M', 'F')
GROUP BY sgc.state
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT sgc.gender) = 2
ORDER BY state
